I will keep the full `wheat-maize` rotation on all `4.1 mu`. I have only a small area, I know this land well, and with a well available I would not leave ground idle or switch crops. For wheat, I will aim for stable yield instead of pushing the field too hard, because in Quzhou water is tight and too much nitrogen is wasteful. I will use an improved wheat variety, give moderate nitrogen with balanced phosphorus and potassium, and plan on two irrigations if spring stays dry: one around jointing and one around grain filling. I will plough before wheat so the soil loosens, residues mix in, and the stand is more even. I expect about `550 kg/mu` on wheat if weather is normal.

For summer maize, I will also plant all `4.1 mu`, using hybrid seed because that is the most reliable way for me to hold yield on a small farm. After wheat harvest I will move fast, use no-tillage or direct seeding into the wheat stubble to save time and moisture, and keep fertilizer moderate because summer rain does part of the work here. I will still keep one irrigation available in reserve through the well in case early growth or tasseling turns dry. I will spray only as needed, usually once or twice for weeds and then for insects or disease if pressure shows up. I expect maize to yield around `650 kg/mu` in a normal year. I’m grounding these decisions in Quzhou/Hebei wheat-maize practice and official guidance on fertilizer and irrigation from China’s agriculture authorities and Hebei reports: https://www.agri.cn/sc/nszd/202309/t20230928_8125583.htm, https://www.agri.cn/zx/xxlb/hb/202603/t20260309_8817365.htm, https://www.moa.gov.cn/govpublic/ZZYGLS/202303/t20230314_6423039.htm, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5290742/
